title: A6 re-enable path cannot restore next_attempt_at — skipped→queued leaves the row invisible to the sweep
evidence:
-- status-only transition (skip, re-enable) never wipes a recorded outcome.
-- Entering any terminal status — or 'skipped', which must leave the cadence
-- — clears next_attempt_at so the sweep never touches the row again.
UPDATE reference_call
SET status = $2::reference_call_status,
    outcome = COALESCE(NULLIF($3, '')::reference_call_outcome, outcome),
    terminal_reason = COALESCE(NULLIF($4, ''), terminal_reason),
    next_attempt_at = CASE
      WHEN $2::reference_call_status IN (
        'skipped', 'partial', 'form_completed', 'unreachable', 'refused',
        'objected', 'manual_recorded', 'failed', 'completed'
      ) THEN NULL
      ELSE next_attempt_at
    END
—and supabase/migrations/20260731222000_create_reference_call.sql:145: `ON reference_call(next_attempt_at) WHERE next_attempt_at IS NOT NULL;`
detail: A6 binds skipped→queued re-enable and the docstring names it, but entering 'skipped' NULLs next_attempt_at and the ELSE branch only preserves it: a re-enabled row stays queued-yet-NULL, outside the sweep's partial index, and no shipped primitive re-arms it.
recommended_fix: Add a next_attempt_at parameter ('' = preserve) to the guarded update, or ship a dedicated re-enable query stamping now(); at minimum remove 're-enable' from the docstring until RC2.3 lands the capability.
